title: Vortex-Number-Controlled Josephson Diode Polarity in Corbino Junctions
abstract: We demonstrate that the polarity of the Josephson diode effect in Corbino Josephson junctions can be deterministically controlled by the vortex number, which arises as a generic consequence of structured spatial inhomogeneity. By solving the continuum Andreev spectral problem, we identify a mechanism in which the vortex number selectively filters specific spatial Fourier harmonics of the local inhomogeneity. This harmonic selection reshapes the amplitudes and relative phases of higher-order Josephson current harmonics, ultimately reversing the critical-current asymmetry. Numerical simulations of both an effective one-dimensional edge model and full two-dimensional lattice models confirm the robustness of this mechanism. Crucially, our results show that a vortex-parity-dependent reversal of diode polarity is not an exclusive signature of Majorana physics, but can emerge generically from geometric and structural inhomogeneities in Corbino junctions.
summary: The paper shows that the diode polarity in Josephson junctions can be controlled by the vortex number ($p$) even without invoking Majorana physics. This control arises from a harmonic-selection rule dictated by structured spatial inhomogeneities in the junction's pairing potential. The findings establish a general principle for engineering non-reciprocal superconducting transport.
main_problem: To determine if vortex-parity-dependent Josephson diode polarity reversal is a unique signature of Majorana physics, or if it can emerge from generic, non-topological mechanisms.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that structured spatial inhomogeneity in Corbino junctions provides a universal mechanism for achieving vortex-parity-dependent alternation of the diode's critical current asymmetry.
method: The analysis uses continuum Andreev spectral theory and perturbation methods to derive a harmonic-selection rule governing how structural modulations affect higher-order Josephson current harmonics.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using Corbino Josephson junctions, described by the continuum Andreev spectral problem Hamiltonian incorporating spatial inhomogeneity $\Delta(	heta)$. The analysis extends from low-dimensional edge models to full two-dimensional lattice simulations.
key_observables: Josephson diode effect (JDE) polarity ($	ext{sgn}(\eta)$), critical currents ($I_{\pm c}$), and the dependence of these on the vortex number $p$.
important_parameters: Vortex number $p$ (integer winding number), structured inhomogeneity $\delta\Delta(	heta)$, and the relative phases/amplitudes of higher-order current harmonics.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a weak spatial modulation ($\delta\Delta \ll \Delta_0$) in the pairing profile, though robustness is shown against finite transparency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Corbino junction geometry and CPR; one figure shows diode polarity dependence on $\phi$ for different profiles, while another compares results across topological and non-topological 2D models showing parity alternation.
paper_structure: The paper develops from establishing the general relationship between diode asymmetry ($\eta$) and current harmonics to deriving a specific harmonic-selection rule based on solving the Andreev spectrum in the presence of structured inhomogeneity, culminating in numerical confirmation across multiple model dimensions.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, non-topological mechanism for observing phenomena often associated with topological superconductivity (like parity dependence), which is highly relevant for understanding engineered superconducting devices and exotic quantum states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Corbino Josephson junction and current-phase re- lation (CPR). (a) Schematic of a Corbino Josephson junc- tion. A perpendicular magnetic field threads the non- superconducting region (N), enclosing a magnetic flux Φ quantized in units of the superconducting flux quantum Φ0 = h/2e. (b) Andreev spectrum and CPR of a homogeneous junction with Φ = Φ0. (c) Corresponding results for an inho- mogeneous junction. The diffuse red spot denotes a Joseph- son vortex, which moves around the annulus as the phase difference ϕ between the inner and outer superconductors is increased.

FIG. 2. The Josephson diode polarity and representative in- homogeneous pairing profile ∆(θ). (a) Diode polarity ob- tained from Eq. (9). (b),(c) Two representative examples of ∆(θ) evaluated on a uniform discretization of θ ∈[0, 2π) with 100 grid points. (b) corresponds to the profile defined in Eq. (3) with nc = 60. (c) shows a two-site perturbation profile, in which the pairing amplitude exhibits opposite-sign deviations from the uniform background at two nearly dia- metrically separated grid points (sites 1 and 50).

Fig. 2(b) shows this profile sampled on a uniform angu- lar grid, corresponding to the discrete values ∆ni used in the numerics. Its dominant feature is two opposite-sign modulations localized in two nearly diametrically oppo- site angular sectors. Motivated by this structure, we further consider a simplified two-site perturbation pro- file with opposite-sign pairing-amplitude perturbations at two nearly diametrically separated grid sites on the ring [Fig. 2(c)]. This reduced profile introduces only small deviations in φj, which weakly renormalize the harmonic phases but do not affect the vortex-number- controlled alternation of the diode polarity.

FIG. 3. Numerical results for effective 1D edge model. (a) Forward and backward critical currents I± c as a function of vortex number p. (b) Corresponding diode polarity η versus p. (c),(d) Current-phase relations for odd and even p, respec- tively. (e),(f) Representative low-energy and quasi-continuum Andreev spectra for p = 1 and p = 2, respectively. The color scale indicates the wavefunction weight on the junc- tion Majorana modes. The inset in (f) shows the sum of the two quasi-continuum branches. Model parameters are v = 1, ∆0 = 0.15, m = 0.6, Ecut = 0.5.

FIG. 4. Numerical results for 2D models. Panels (a),(c) show the forward and backward critical currents I± c and diode po- larity η, respectively, for a non-topological Corbino Josephson junction. The model parameters are W = 400, L = 2, t = 20, µ = 10, ∆= 1, nc = 300. Panels (b),(d) show the corresponding results for a topological junction. The model parameters are W = 300, L = 2, t = 300, M0 = 20, M1 = 300, mz = 20, µ = 5, ∆= 10, nc = 200.
